items.label: Used correct opening spiel and introduced themselves

lv.3: full correct spiel, clear intro
lv.2: greeted but missed one element
lv.1: wrong or skipped entirely

items.label: Maintained friendly, professional tone; avoided jargon; managed dead air with updates

lv.3: warm, composed, plain language, no unmanaged silences
lv.2: mostly professional, minor lapses or brief dead air
lv.1: abrupt, heavy jargon, or long unmanaged silences

items.label: Showed empathy and composure; did not become defensive on difficult calls

lv.3: consistent empathy, de-escalated naturally
lv.2: attempted but inconsistent
lv.1: defensive or dismissive

items.tip: Mark 3 if no difficult moment arose on this call.

items.label: Conducted the interaction in an understandable manner; understood the client's concern and communicated the resolution clearly.

lv.3: clear communication throughout, client understood the issue and resolution
lv.2: mostly understood the client and communicated the right things, but has identifiable points for improvement
lv.1: did not address the concern directly; English communication was unclear or caused confusion

items.label: Actively listened, asked only relevant questions, and gathered all necessary information before proceeding

lv.3: all key info gathered efficiently, no redundant probing
lv.2: got main facts, some unnecessary questions or missed follow-ups
lv.1: proceeded without adequate info or excessive re-probing

items.label: Root Cause Triage & Fault Attribution- Correctly identified what went wrong and who is at fault

lv.3: Correct root cause and accurate fault attribution
lv.2: Identified the issue but misread root cause or fault attribution
lv.1: Wrong diagnosis or no attribution made

items.label: Immediate resolution - Took the right short-term action given the situation

lv.3: confident, accurate
lv.2: general knowledge, gaps on edge cases
lv.1: clear misunderstanding

items.tip: Note in comments whether error was product or process.

items.label: Long-term Solution- Identified and actioned a long-term fix (product improvement, process change) or escalated to the right team to do so.

lv.3: Long-term path identified and actioned or escalated to the right owner
lv.2: Root cause acknowledged but long-term path vague or incomplete
lv.1: No long-term path attempted or escalated

lv.3: resolved independently OR escalated only where truly necessary

lv.1: passed off without attempting resolution

items.label: Edge Case Judgment During Resolution: knowing when to pause and confirm with the client before proceeding (vs. resolving on assumption and getting it wrong)

lv.3: Correctly identified the edge case and confirmed with the client first; avoided a wrong or incomplete resolution
lv.2: Noticed the ambiguity but proceeded without confirming, or confirmed but inefficiently (e.g., multiple unnecessary back-and-forths)
lv.1: Resolved on assumption when the situation clearly needed client confirmation first; led to wrong resolution or follow-up rework

items.label: Proactive Client Outreach — knowing when to reach back out to win back a customer, offer compensation, or flag an issue you found proactively — and doing so vs. just closing the case

lv.3: Proactively reached out without being prompted; used the right channel and addressed the issue appropriately (compensation, win-back, or flagging)
lv.2: Identified the need for follow-up but action was incomplete, delayed, or used the wrong channel
lv.1: Missed a clear opportunity — case closed without appropriate outreach on a situation where client sentiment or the issue clearly warranted it
